sections.h2: What is Macon County, Illinois, and who bills its property tax?
sections.html:
Macon County is the Decatur area of central Illinois, formed in 1829 and named for Nathaniel Macon. Decatur is the county seat and largest city, and Macon and Maroa are the other cities. The county covers about 581 square miles of flat glacial plain and calls itself the Heart of Illinois. Neighbors are De Witt, Piatt, Moultrie, Shelby, Christian, Sangamon and Logan counties. The family of Abraham Lincoln moved to the county in 1830.

The County Treasurer collects about 55,000 tax bills a year for schools, libraries, parks, municipalities and the county. The office is in the Macon County Office Building at 141 South Main Street, Room 302, Decatur, and its phone is 217-424-1426. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, excluding legal holidays. Bills can be paid online at maconcountyil.us, and the payment site's help line is 844-400-8880.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Macon County housing?
sections.html:
Macon County is losing population: the Census Bureau estimates 99,300 residents for July 1, 2025, down 4.5% from the April 2020 base. In the 2020 count, 83.0% of residents lived in urban areas.

sections.h2: How does Macon County assess a home?
sections.html:
The Supervisor of Assessments helps the township assessors, administers exemptions, keeps the cadastral maps and property record cards, applies equalization factors, sends assessment notices, publishes assessments in local newspapers and serves as clerk of the Board of Review. The office is at 141 South Main Street, Room 401, phone 217-424-1364, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

Illinois sets the target at 33 1/3% of market value outside Cook County. You can find your assessment on the county website, on a mailed notice when the property changed or the township is in its general reassessment year, in the newspaper publication, on your tax bill, or by calling the office. Property record cards can be printed by address and PIN at $.35 a page. Real estate transfer declarations are also available to view in the office for appeals that rely on sales.

Your bill equals assessed value minus exemptions, times the rates of each district serving the parcel. A house a block away can have a different set of districts, so comparing bills with a neighbor can mislead.

sections.h2: What is the deadline to appeal a Macon County assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal to affect the current assessment year must be filed on or before 30 calendar days after the date of publication. Each township has its own publication date. The county's 2026 notice gives October 10, 2026 as the publication date for the 2026 assessments and November 9, 2026 as the deadline to file with the Board of Review, so that window has closed. The county's FAQ warns that by state statute an appeal cannot be accepted after the deadline.

The Board of Review has three members appointed by the County Board. It hears 800 to 1,000 appeals in a tax year and generally finishes hearings by the end of February. The county's FAQ lists the evidence that carries weight:

  • A market analysis from a licensed realtor
  • A certified appraisal
  • A comparable sheet
  • A closing or settlement statement
  • Pictures

You choose between an equity argument, which compares assessments of comparable nearby homes, and a market value argument, which needs recent sales. The Board will tell you it has no jurisdiction over your tax bill, so a hearing that only says taxes are too high goes nowhere.

sections.h2: What happens after a Macon County Board of Review decision?
sections.html:
The Board comes into session June 1 of the year, and all communications are by mail, so put the correct mailing address on the complaint form. You can receive one of three replies: agreement with your evidence, a tentative value with 10 days to ask in writing for a hearing, or a hearing notice. A hearing can be rescheduled only once.

A final notice usually goes out in January. From the postmark date on that notice you have 30 days to file with the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board, where the case starts fresh and new evidence is allowed. After that, the next step is a court action, and the county suggests contacting an attorney. The Board also acts on property omitted from the assessment roll and must notify the owner first.

sections.h2: When are Macon County tax bills due and what is the penalty?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in May. The first installment is due 30 days after the bill is mailed, and the second is due September 1, moving to the next working day if that date falls on a weekend or Labor Day. Illinois taxes are billed and collected a year behind, so the bill you pay in a given calendar year is for the prior tax year. You receive one bill a year with two coupons, and no separate bill is mailed for the second installment.

The Treasurer's page says Illinois statutes require a penalty of 1 1/2% per month or part of a month on payments made after the due date, and that even a payment one day late takes the penalty. Call the office for the exact figure. A bill that fails to arrive does not remove the obligation. Many owners pay from a mortgage escrow, so confirm with your servicer whether it will pay, to avoid a duplicate payment or none at all.

Mobile home tax is billed differently. Bills are mailed in April, the tax is due in one installment within 60 days, and after that a penalty of $25 per month or part of a month applies, up to $100. A $10 tax certification is required before a mobile home is sold or moved.

sections.h2: How does the Macon County tax sale work?
sections.html:
After the second installment payments are posted, a delinquent notice goes by certified mail to the billing address, with $10 added to cover mailing and newspaper publication. The Treasurer also publishes the owner's name, parcel number and amount due in a county newspaper. Unpaid taxes are then offered at the annual tax sale, where tax buyers bid an interest percentage beginning at 9% and bidding downward. The buyer bidding the lowest interest wins a certificate. The buyer purchases the tax, not the house.

The Treasurer's page describes at least 30 and not more than 36 months to redeem for an owner-occupied property, with redemption made at the County Clerk's office. The redemption amount includes the tax sold, penalty, publication cost, sale costs, any costs the buyer incurred and interest, bid up to 9% and compounded every six months. State law, at 35 ILCS 200/21-350, generally gives 3 years from the sale, with exceptions, so ask the Clerk for the exact deadline stated on your certificate.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Macon County owner claim?
sections.html:
State law sets the homestead amounts, and Macon County is not next to a county of 3,000,000 or more people, so the lower figures apply. The general homestead exemption is up to $6,000 off equalized assessed value (35 ILCS 200/15-175), and the senior citizens exemption is up to $5,000 for owners 65 or older who occupy the home (35 ILCS 200/15-170). Applications and questions go to the Supervisor of Assessments.

The Treasurer's office also administers the Senior Citizens' Real Estate Tax Deferral Program. Separately, the Supervisor of Assessments takes applications for the affordable housing program under 35 ILCS 200/10-260, with a filing deadline of September 1 of each assessment year.

When you buy or sell, check with the title company on who owes the tax. New owners should file a change of address form with the Treasurer by March 15, because the deed's address reaches that office only after a lag.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Macon County?
faqs.a: Pay online at maconcountyil.us or at the Treasurer's office, 141 South Main Street, Room 302, Decatur. Call 217-424-1426 with bill questions, or the payment site help line at 844-400-8880 for technical trouble.

faqs.q: When did the 2026 Macon County appeal window close?
faqs.a: It closed November 9, 2026. The county announced October 10, 2026 as the 2026 publication date, and the Board of Review rule allows 30 calendar days from publication.

faqs.q: Does Macon County mail a separate bill for the second installment?
faqs.a: No. You get a single bill each year with two tear-off coupons, and the second installment is due September 1, or the next working day when that date falls on a weekend or Labor Day.

faqs.q: Does a tax sale mean I lose my Macon County house?
faqs.a: Not at the sale itself. Tax buyers purchase the unpaid tax, and the owner may redeem by paying the redemption amount at the County Clerk's office.

faqs.q: What does it cost to certify mobile home taxes in Macon County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer charges a $10 fee for tax certification, by cash or check only. Taxes must be paid to date, the original title must be presented, and the office needs the seller's and buyer's names and addresses.
